newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ekran chief says Bakun differences remain.
newsitem.headline: Ekran chief says Bakun differences remain.

text.p: Ekran Bhd's chairman said on Thursday differences between his company and ABB Asea Brown Boveri over the $6.18 billion Bakun dam project were yet to be resolved.

Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khiing briefly spoke to reporters at his headquarters, after a five-hour meeting between the two companies. When asked whether differences over the project had been resolved, he said: "Not yet".

Ekran, who was awarded the Bakun hydroelectric dam project in Sarawak state on Borneo island, has given the $5.5 billion engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract to ABB and Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos o Obras (CBPO).
Ting said the next round of discussions with ABB would take place "in two weeks' time". He did not clarify the nature of the differences.

He said representatives of the other key shareholders, which include the Sarawak Electricity Supply Corporation, national power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd, state pension fund Employees Provident Fund, and government investment arm Khazannah Holdings Bhd, would have to confer with their respective boards.
Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said last week that there were "major disagreements" over the terms of the agreement between Ekran and ABB.

An advisor to Ting had earlier confirmed to reporters that Bakun Hydroelectric Corp Bhd (BHC), the operating company of the Bakun project was "seeking clarification of some of the terms (of the EPC agreement) from ABB."
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Tuesday there was no dispute between the companies involved in the project, only differing personal opinions.
